decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering the selected kerning, common baseline, E/L height reference, and second-V cap-height hierarchy.

The same-message MODIFY establishes an exact E/L height match to the second V’s left arm, superseding the older instruction merely to reduce the E and L slightly; the obsolete e_and_l_scale key must be removed.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
This round was very productive, and my preference is the common-baseline composition in Variation B with its tighter kerning.

Right now, the second V still appears noticeably smaller than the surrounding letters. For the next revision, please scale the Es and Ls so their height matches the height established by the second V’s left arm, while keeping the second V’s right arm as the only element extending slightly above them to serve as the intentional signature detail. Please also ensure that the accent is a perfect copy/paste of the Hero V’s right arm.

value_updates.e_and_l_height_reference: Scale the E and L forms so their height matches the height established by the second V’s left arm.

decisions.reason: The source changes the relative heights of the second V and surrounding letters but does not alter the approved Hero V geometry or its locked revision policy.
The instruction that the accent remain a perfect copy of the Hero V right arm reaffirms the existing shared-terminal rule and does not change the terminal requirement.
The requested perfect copy/paste relationship is already fully represented by the candidate’s literal derivation and exact-curve copy requirements.
The source concerns geometric scale and height hierarchy, not the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The source applies existing brand principles to specific wordmark geometry without changing the broader brand-expression requirement.
Adjusting the second V and surrounding letter heights does not change the decision to use a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
